hints.title: Correlating Start and End Activity Records
hints.text: Each machine runs processes where each process has a start record and an end record.

hints.title: Joining Start and End Records
hints.text: join the activity table with itself on machine_id and process_id to align the start and end timestamps side by side.

hints.title: Averaging Processing Times
hints.text: filter for start activity on the left and end activity on the right, compute their difference, and aggregate with avg rounded to 3 decimal places grouped by machine_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT a.machine_id, ROUND(AVG(b.timestamp - a.timestamp), 3) AS processing_time
FROM Activity a
JOIN Activity b ON a.machine_id = b.machine_id AND a.process_id = b.process_id AND a.activity_type = 'start' AND b.activity_type = 'end'
GROUP BY a.machine_id;
```

complexity.notes: Self-join on composite machine and process key groups event pairs in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries for every row require scanning the activity table repeatedly in quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A self-join on machine and process ID runs in linear time with indexed lookups and minimal temporary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should demonstrate self-joining start and end events or using conditional aggregation with CASE WHEN.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def get_average_time(activity: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    start = activity[activity['activity_type'] == 'start']
    end = activity[activity['activity_type'] == 'end']
    merged = start.merge(end, on=['machine_id', 'process_id'], suffixes=('_start', '_end'))
    merged['diff'] = merged['timestamp_end'] - merged['timestamp_start']
    res = merged.groupby('machine_id')['diff'].mean().round(3).reset_index()
    res.rename(columns={'diff': 'processing_time'}, inplace=True)
    return res
solutions.approach: Average Time of Process per Machine pandas Solution
